description: Salt Marsh Habitat Restoration on Parker River National Wildlife Refuge is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by USFWS, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. From the 1600s to the 1900s, high density drainage networks and berms were constructed to increase crop production and reduce mosquito populations. Lack of maintenance caused these drainage ditches to clog up over time, increasing water retention in the marsh. Coverage: Parker River National Wildlife Refuge (2024). The toolkit gives Parker River National Wildlife Refuge as the location, 2024 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
